- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 5–10% in early horizon.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >15% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 3–8%.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 40), model overreacts; adjust forecast to align with recent 7-day moving average.
- When sentiment flips from negative to positive, model delays correction; forecast should begin to converge toward true trend within 3–5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates downward trends; add 2–5% buffer for negative sentiment or low volatility periods.
- If true outcome shows sudden drop after spike, model fails to recognize “rebound exhaustion”; reduce forecast by 5–10% in 10–15 day window.
